title: Unified resilience and retry spec for inter-service failovers and SDKs
creator: Leah Cheng
description:
Goal: Create a single, practical specification and reference implementation that standardizes retry, timeout, backoff, hedged requests, idempotency key behavior, circuit breaker thresholds, and load-shedding signals across Redwood services and public SDKs. The spec should be prescriptive enough for services to interoperate (preserve client intent and SLOs) and permissive enough to allow platform-level overrides for multi-region failover and Dedicated/Private deployments.

Why now: Multiple incidents and recent on-call postmortems show divergent retry behaviors across services cause cascading retries, wasted GPU cycles, and bursty load during region flaps. SDK implementations vary by language; client teams are confused about recommended idempotency surfaces and hedging semantics. We need a canonical contract to reduce operational blast radius and give the Console/Optimize teams consistent observability signals for cost accounting and SLO-aware routing.

Scope:
- Spec document describing request lifecycle: client timeout vs service deadline, idempotency key surface, hedged request semantics, and how to attach a routing policy for failover.
- SDK changes (JS/Go/Python) to add a common retries/backoff module and idempotency header convention.
- Runtime changes to accept client hedging tokens, expose circuit-breaker state in trace spans, and respect load-shedding hints from control plane.
- Observability: telemetry fields to emit for retries, hedged events, load-shed decisions, circuit-breaker transitions, and associated token-level cost tags.
- Backwards compatibility plan and rollout runbook.

Non-goals: Rewriting per-service retry logic from scratch during this ticket; migrating all services in one sprint. This ticket produces the spec, a reference SDK implementation, and an onboarding checklist for teams to migrate incrementally.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical spec (Confluence) exists and is approved by Resilience and SDK leads.
JS/Go SDK libraries include new retry module with documented idempotency header convention and unit tests demonstrating hedged request behavior.
Runtime accepts hedging token and emits hedged request telemetry; circuit-breaker state exported to tracing and metrics.
Rollout runbook covers canary migration steps, per-service data collection, and rollback criteria.
Two pilot services (inference runtime and routing) have migrated and demonstrated reduced retry amplification in load tests.
decisions: Use 'x-rw-idempotency-key' as the standard idempotency header for all RPCs and HTTP endpoints.
Hedged requests allowed only for non-mutating read paths by default; a service opt-in flag required for write paths.
Client timeouts are advisory; services must enforce a service-side deadline header 'x-rw-deadline-ms' to bound server work and avoid unbounded KV cache growth.
Circuit breaker thresholds will be expressed in two dimensions: error-rate over 1m and queue-latency P99; both are configurable by service with platform-recommended defaults.
Backoff policy default: jittered exponential with base 50ms, factor 2, max backoff 2s for transient token-level errors; explicit 'fast-fail' codes for auth/fatal errors.
notes: Trade-offs: Aggressive hedging can reduce tail latency but increases total token spend. Spec includes a 'hedging_budget' parameter on routes to cap token overhead per minute.
Load-shedding signals: runtime will return 429 + 'x-rw-shed-reason' with machine-readable codes to let SDKs choose graceful degradation vs retry suppression.
Idempotency semantics: server-side deduplication window default 5 minutes for inference generate endpoints, configurable per model to support long-running chains where clients may reconnect.
Cross-region failover: include 'prefer-region' and 'fallback-regions' in routing metadata; client SDK can attach a hint but control plane may override for capacity and SLO reasons.

Week 2: Merge reference SDK module and runtime hedging acceptance; add telemetry fields.
Week 3: Pilot two services and run synthetic multi-region failover tests; measure retry amplification and token overhead.
Week 4: Iterate on thresholds and publish rollout runbook for broader migration.
